extraction.name: Stanford Question Answering Dataset (SQuAD) v1.0
extraction.description: A reading comprehension dataset consisting of 107,785 question-answer pairs on 536 Wikipedia articles, where answers are text spans from the corresponding passages.
extraction.creator: Pranav Rajpurkar, Jian Zhang, Konstantin Lopyrev, Percy Liang
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was collected in three stages: curating passages from Wikipedia, crowdsourcing question-answer pairs on those passages, and obtaining additional answers for development and test questions.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Manual Human Curator, Crowdsourcing, Self-reporting
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Over the development and test sets, 2.6% of questions were marked unanswerable by at least one of the additional crowdworkers.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: English Wikipedia articles; top 10,000 articles by Project Nayuki's Wikipedia internal PageRanks were used to sample 536 articles uniformly at random, and paragraphs were extracted from those articles.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: From each sampled Wikipedia article, individual paragraphs were extracted, images/figures/tables were stripped away, and paragraphs shorter than 500 characters were discarded.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Articles were partitioned randomly into training (80%), development (10%), and test (10%) sets. Candidate answers were restricted to constituency spans generated by Stanford CoreNLP during modeling.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Crowdworkers on Daemo/Amazon Mechanical Turk wrote questions for each paragraph and highlighted answer spans in the paragraph. For development and test sets, additional crowdworkers were shown the questions and paragraphs and asked to select the shortest span answering each question, or mark the question unanswerable if no span answered it.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Daemo platform with Amazon Mechanical Turk as backend
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: At least 2 additional answers were collected for each development and test question. Human performance was evaluated using the second answer as prediction and the remaining answers as ground truth. The paper reports that 2.6% of questions were marked unanswerable by at least one additional crowdworker.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: At least 3 answers per development/test question (original answer plus at least 2 additional answers); up to 5 questions per paragraph were created by crowdworkers.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Crowdworkers were required to be located in the United States or Canada, have a 97% HIT acceptance rate, and a minimum of 1000 HITs.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Stanford CoreNLP was used to generate constituency parses, POS tags, dependency parses, and NER tags for analysis and candidate span generation.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Version 1.0 was released and made freely available at https://stanford-qa.com. The paper does not specify an update schedule, maintainers, or deprecation policy.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Crowdworker location (United States or Canada) and work history requirements (HIT acceptance rate and minimum HIT count) were collected as annotator eligibility criteria; no sensitive attributes of the dataset content are described.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is intended to advance machine reading comprehension and natural language understanding research by providing a large, high-quality benchmark.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The paper notes that the dataset covers a wide range of topics and answer types, but does not explicitly discuss dataset bias.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset uses span-based answers, which are more constrained than free-form answers. Some questions are ambiguous or not uniquely answerable. The paper also notes that candidate answers are restricted to constituency spans, placing an effective ceiling on model accuracy.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, development, and testing of machine reading comprehension/question answering systems; evaluation of exact match and F1 performance.
